question: Milk appears white in the surrounding of white light because the particles in milk are _______ than the wavelength of different colours in white light that falls on it, and all colours of white light are scattered by _________ amount(s).
solution:
The correct answer is __**larger, about the same.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Milk **appears white in the surrounding of **white light **because the particles in milk are **larger than the wavelength **of different colours in white light that falls on it.
 
• This means that the light waves **scatter in all directions** when they come in contact with the particles in milk, making the **milk appear white.**
 
• Larger is the correct answer as the size of the particles in milk is larger than the wavelength of **different colours** in white light.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Milk** is an example of a **colloid**, which is a mixture where one substance is** dispersed** in another substance.
 
• In the case of milk, the **fat and protein particles** are dispersed in water.
 
• The size of the particles in milk can vary **depending **on the type of milk and the processing it undergoes.
 
• For example, whole milk has **larger particles** than skim milk.
 
• The **scattering of light** by particles in a colloid is called the **Tyndall effect, **which is used to determine if a mixture is a **solution or a colloid**.
 
• If the mixture **scatters light**, it is a **colloid.**
 
• The Tyndall effect is also used in various industries, such as **pharmaceuticals,** to determine the **size and concentration of particles** in a colloid.
